pathway.name: Suspected stable angina (chest pain assessment)
pathway.population: Adults presenting to a GP with stable chest pain suggestive of angina
pathway.summary: GP assessment, ECG and bloods, then cardiology referral for most patients, with CT coronary angiography or stress testing and a small share going on to invasive angiography.

steps.label: CT coronary angiography
steps.note: Anatomical test of choice for low to intermediate risk

steps.label: Invasive coronary angiogram (same-day admission)
steps.note: For high-risk CT or stress results

name: Stable coronary artery disease, ongoing management

pathway.name: Stable coronary artery disease, ongoing management
pathway.population: Adults with established stable coronary artery disease
pathway.summary: Secondary prevention in general practice with yearly cardiology review, lipid and renal monitoring, and a small annual chance of admission or revascularisation.

steps.label: Cardiologist initial consultation
steps.note: Annual cardiology review (charged as initial when referral renewed)

steps.label: Admission for angina or chest pain

pathway.name: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
pathway.population: Adults with STEMI managed in a public hospital
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Emergency reperfusion, usually primary PCI, then dual antiplatelet therapy, secondary prevention and cardiac rehabilitation over the first year.

steps.label: Emergency department attendance
steps.note: Some patients go straight to the catheter laboratory

steps.label: Admission with PCI for AMI, minor complexity
Admission with PCI for AMI, major complexity

pathway.name: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI)
pathway.population: Adults admitted with NSTEMI to a public hospital
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Admission with early invasive angiography for most patients, PCI or bypass where indicated, then secondary prevention.

pathway.name: Unstable angina
pathway.population: Adults presenting with unstable angina
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Emergency assessment and admission, with angiography and PCI for a share of patients, followed by secondary prevention.

pathway.name: Elective PCI for stable angina
pathway.population: Adults with stable angina referred for elective PCI
pathway.summary: Planned PCI admission, six to twelve months of clopidogrel with aspirin, and cardiology follow-up.

pathway.name: Coronary artery bypass grafting (elective)
pathway.population: Adults with multivessel coronary disease referred for bypass surgery
pathway.summary: Surgical review, planned bypass admission, then rehabilitation and secondary prevention.

pathway.name: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD)
pathway.population: Adults, mostly women, presenting with SCAD
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Admission for acute coronary syndrome managed conservatively in most cases, imaging follow-up, beta blocker and rehabilitation.

pathway.name: Familial hypercholesterolaemia
pathway.population: Adults with a new diagnosis of heterozygous FH
pathway.summary: Lipid specialist or cardiology assessment, high-intensity statin with ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitor for those not at target, and lipid monitoring.

steps.label: Evolocumab 140 mg
steps.note: If LDL above target despite oral therapy

pathway.name: Atrial fibrillation, new diagnosis
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed non-valvular AF
pathway.summary: Diagnosis in general practice or ED, echocardiogram and bloods, anticoagulation for most patients, rate or rhythm control, and cardioversion or ablation for a minority.

steps.label: Arrhythmia admission
steps.note: Rate control or new diagnosis admission

steps.label: Oral anticoagulant (priced as apixaban 5 mg)
steps.note: Share prescribed any oral anticoagulant in Australian general practice

prob.ref: Bezabhe WM et al. Ten-year trends in the use of oral anticoagulants in Australian general practice patients with AF. Front Pharmacol 2021;12:586370. 52.0% prescribed an OAC in 2018 (39.5% in 2009; 65.6% in top practice quintile)

steps.label: Rivaroxaban 20 mg
steps.note: Set to 0: all anticoagulant use is counted in the step above

prob.ref: Included in the anticoagulant share above

pathway.name: Atrial flutter
pathway.population: Adults with typical atrial flutter
pathway.summary: Rate control and anticoagulation, with catheter ablation of the cavotricuspid isthmus for about half of patients.

pathway.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
pathway.population: Adults with recurrent paroxysmal SVT
pathway.summary: Emergency treatment of episodes, cardiology assessment and monitoring, and catheter ablation for many patients.

pathway.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
pathway.population: Young people and adults with a symptomatic accessory pathway
pathway.summary: Cardiology assessment, monitoring and echocardiography, with catheter ablation for most symptomatic patients.

name: Ventricular tachycardia with structural heart disease

pathway.name: Ventricular tachycardia with structural heart disease
pathway.population: Adults with sustained VT and reduced ventricular function
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Emergency admission, cardiac MRI, ICD implantation for most patients, antiarrhythmic therapy and VT ablation for some.

name: Complete heart block or symptomatic bradycardia

pathway.name: Complete heart block or symptomatic bradycardia
pathway.population: Older adults with high-grade AV block
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Emergency presentation and admission for permanent pacemaker in almost all patients, then device follow-up.

pathway.name: Sick sinus syndrome
pathway.population: Older adults with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction
pathway.summary: Monitoring to link symptoms to bradycardia, with pacemaker implantation for about half of patients.

pathway.name: Long QT syndrome
pathway.population: Children and adults with congenital long QT syndrome
pathway.summary: Specialist assessment, genetic testing, beta blocker therapy, monitoring and an ICD for a small high-risk group.

pathway.name: Brugada syndrome
pathway.population: Adults with a Brugada type 1 ECG pattern
pathway.summary: Specialist risk assessment, genetic testing in some, and an ICD for patients with arrhythmic syncope or cardiac arrest.

pathway.name: Syncope, suspected cardiac cause
pathway.population: Adults presenting with unexplained syncope
pathway.summary: Emergency assessment, admission for higher-risk patients, echocardiography and rhythm monitoring, an implantable loop recorder for recurrent unexplained events and pacing for a few.

pathway.name: Palpitations
pathway.population: Adults presenting to a GP with palpitations
pathway.summary: GP assessment with ECG, bloods and ambulatory monitoring, echocardiography for some and cardiology referral for a minority.

name: Palpitations with a 14-day ECG patch (Lubdub scenario)

pathway.name: Palpitations with a 14-day ECG patch (Lubdub scenario)
pathway.population: Adults presenting to a GP with palpitations
pathway.summary: Same as the palpitations pathway, except the 7-day ambulatory ECG is replaced by a 14-day wearable ECG patch, and slightly fewer patients are referred to a cardiologist because longer monitoring catches more episodes. The patch is priced at the break-even point, the price at which total cost per patient equals current care ($468).

prob.ref: Replaced by the patch in this scenario

steps.label: Lubdub 14-day ECG patch
steps.note: Price set at break-even; Lubdub has not published a price

price.ref: Break-even price: total equals current care

prob.ref: Same share as the 7-day ECG it replaces
Assumed: longer monitoring gives a diagnosis in more patients, so fewer referrals (current care 30%)

pathway.name: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest survivor
pathway.population: Adults surviving to hospital admission after cardiac arrest
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Intensive care with ventilation, coronary angiography and PCI where indicated, ICD for many survivors, and rehabilitation.

name: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, new diagnosis

pathway.name: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, new diagnosis
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed HFrEF
pathway.summary: Diagnosis with natriuretic peptide and echocardiogram, admission for about half of patients, four-pillar medical therapy, close monitoring, and device therapy for some.

name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

pathway.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
pathway.population: Older adults with HFpEF
pathway.summary: Diagnosis with natriuretic peptide and echocardiogram, diuretics and SGLT2 inhibitor, management of comorbidities, and admission for a third of patients.

pathway.name: Acute decompensated heart failure admission
pathway.population: Adults admitted with acute decompensated heart failure
pathway.summary: Emergency presentation and admission, non-invasive ventilation for some, early post-discharge review and a high readmission rate.

pathway.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
pathway.population: Adults with non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy
pathway.summary: As for HFrEF, plus cardiac MRI, genetic testing and family screening referral, with ICD for persistent severe dysfunction.

pathway.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
pathway.population: Adults with a new diagnosis of HCM
pathway.summary: Imaging with echocardiogram and cardiac MRI, rhythm monitoring and exercise testing for risk stratification, genetic testing, beta blocker, myosin inhibitor for some with obstruction, and ICD for high-risk patients.

steps.label: Mavacamten
steps.note: Obstructive HCM not controlled on first-line therapy

pathway.name: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM)
pathway.population: Older adults with ATTR cardiomyopathy
pathway.summary: Diagnosis with echocardiogram, cardiac MRI, light-chain tests and nuclear scintigraphy, tafamidis for eligible patients, diuretics and heart failure admissions.

pathway.name: Acute myocarditis
pathway.population: Adults presenting with acute myocarditis
pathway.summary: Emergency presentation with chest pain, admission with troponin monitoring, cardiac MRI for diagnosis, and echocardiographic follow-up.

pathway.name: Aortic stenosis, moderate (surveillance)
pathway.population: Adults with moderate aortic stenosis
pathway.summary: Annual echocardiogram and cardiology review in most patients, with progression to intervention for a small share.

pathway.name: Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis
pathway.population: Older adults with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis
pathway.summary: Heart team assessment with CT and coronary angiography, then TAVI for most and surgical valve replacement for younger or lower-risk patients.

pathway.name: Severe mitral regurgitation
pathway.population: Adults with severe primary or secondary mitral regurgitation
pathway.summary: Echocardiography including transoesophageal study, surgical repair for many, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for high-risk patients, and heart failure therapy.

pathway.name: Rheumatic mitral stenosis
pathway.population: Adults with significant rheumatic mitral stenosis
pathway.summary: Echocardiography, anticoagulation for those in AF, rate control, and balloon valvotomy or surgery for severe disease.

pathway.name: Infective endocarditis
pathway.population: Adults admitted with infective endocarditis
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Prolonged admission for intravenous antibiotics, transoesophageal echocardiography, valve surgery for about a quarter, and outpatient follow-up.

steps.label: Transoesophageal echocardiogram
steps.note: Private patients only; public TOE is inside the admission

pathway.name: Rheumatic heart disease (secondary prophylaxis)
pathway.population: Children and young adults with rheumatic heart disease on secondary prophylaxis
pathway.summary: Four-weekly benzathine penicillin injections in primary care, yearly echocardiogram and specialist review.

steps.label: GP or clinic visits for injections

pathway.name: Bicuspid aortic valve
pathway.population: Adults with bicuspid aortic valve without severe dysfunction
pathway.summary: Echocardiographic surveillance of the valve and aorta, CT or MRI of the aorta for some, and blood pressure control.

pathway.name: Atrial septal defect (child)
pathway.population: Children with a haemodynamically significant secundum ASD
pathway.summary: Paediatric cardiology assessment with echocardiography, transcatheter device closure for most significant defects and surgery for a few.

pathway.name: Ventricular septal defect (child)
pathway.population: Children with a ventricular septal defect
pathway.summary: Echocardiographic surveillance for most, with surgical repair for large defects causing heart failure.

pathway.name: Patent ductus arteriosus (child)
pathway.population: Infants and children with a persistent PDA after the neonatal period
pathway.summary: Echocardiographic assessment and transcatheter closure for most haemodynamically significant ducts.

pathway.name: Repaired tetralogy of Fallot (adult follow-up)
pathway.population: Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot
pathway.summary: Adult congenital clinic review with echocardiography, cardiac MRI and rhythm monitoring, and pulmonary valve replacement for a few each year.

pathway.name: Coarctation of the aorta
pathway.population: Children and adults with significant coarctation
pathway.summary: Imaging of the aorta, surgical repair in infants and stenting in older patients, and blood pressure follow-up.

pathway.name: Kawasaki disease
pathway.population: Children admitted with Kawasaki disease
pathway.summary: Admission for IVIG and aspirin, serial echocardiograms to look for coronary aneurysms, and longer-term follow-up for the few with aneurysms.

steps.label: Admission (other circulatory)
steps.note: IVIG in hospital; paediatric adjustment applied

pathway.name: Acute pericarditis
pathway.population: Adults with acute idiopathic or viral pericarditis
pathway.summary: Emergency assessment, colchicine with an anti-inflammatory for three months, echocardiogram, and admission for higher-risk features.

pathway.name: Pericardial effusion requiring drainage
pathway.population: Adults with a large effusion or tamponade
pathway.summary: Emergency admission for pericardiocentesis or surgical drainage, investigation of the cause, and echocardiographic follow-up.

pathway.name: Pulmonary embolism
pathway.population: Adults with acute pulmonary embolism
pathway.summary: Emergency diagnosis with CT pulmonary angiography, admission for most, anticoagulation for at least three to six months, and follow-up.

steps.label: CT pulmonary angiography (community or private)
steps.note: Scans done in a public ED are inside the ED price

pathway.name: Deep vein thrombosis
pathway.population: Adults with proximal lower-limb DVT
pathway.summary: Duplex ultrasound diagnosis, outpatient anticoagulation for most patients, and a small share admitted.

pathway.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension
pathway.summary: Echocardiography and right heart catheterisation, specialist PAH centre care, dual oral therapy for most patients, and natriuretic peptide monitoring.

pathway.name: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (surveillance)
pathway.population: Older adults with a small to medium AAA
pathway.summary: Ultrasound surveillance, vascular surgeon review, cardiovascular risk management, and repair for those reaching the size threshold.

pathway.name: Acute type A aortic dissection
pathway.population: Adults with acute type A dissection
pathway.horizon: 12 months from the index event, including the index admission
pathway.summary: Emergency CT diagnosis and surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, intensive care, then lifelong aortic imaging and blood pressure control.

steps.label: Aortic surgery with bypass pump, major complexity

pathway.name: Peripheral artery disease (intermittent claudication)
pathway.population: Adults with symptomatic lower-limb peripheral artery disease
pathway.summary: Arterial duplex, secondary prevention with statin and antiplatelet, supervised exercise advice, and revascularisation for a minority.

pathway.name: Hypertension, new diagnosis
pathway.population: Adults with newly diagnosed primary hypertension
pathway.summary: Confirmation with ambulatory blood pressure, baseline ECG and bloods, one or two first-line agents, and GP follow-up.

pathway.name: Resistant hypertension
pathway.population: Adults with blood pressure above target on three agents
pathway.summary: Specialist assessment for secondary causes, ambulatory monitoring, renal imaging, echocardiography, and a fourth agent such as spironolactone.

pathway.name: Hypertension in pregnancy (chronic or gestational)
pathway.population: Pregnant women with chronic or gestational hypertension
pathway.summary: Antenatal blood pressure monitoring with labetalol or nifedipine, laboratory monitoring for pre-eclampsia, and admission for a share. Obstetric and birth costs are excluded.

steps.label: GP consultations
steps.note: Shared antenatal care visits for blood pressure
